thread.title_full: Pflugerville woman sentenced for defrauding PPP Loan program - NewsBreak

author: Matt McGovern
title: Pflugerville woman sentenced for defrauding PPP Loan program - NewsBreak
text:
By Matt McGovern ,
8 hours ago
WACO, Texas ( FOX 44 ) – A Pflugerville woman was sentenced in a Waco federal court to 21 months in prison for submitting fraudulent Paycheck Protection Loan (PPP) applications.
This was announced by U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas on Wednesday. According to court documents, 34-year-old Aisha Jackson, was doing business as Logo Boosters on March 10, 2021. She submitted a PPP application to a loan processor.
According to the Department of Justice (DoJ), the application contained false statements and documentation including a fabricated voided check stub. Federal agents found Jackson opened the bank account reflected on the check stub in her own name, but used the stolen social security number of a minor victim.
Bank records showed that no checks were written from the account. A further investigation revealed that Jackson used the same victim’s social security number in 2016 to get a vehicle loan.
The DoJ says agents also found Jackson submitted a false 2019 Schedule C, Profit or Loss from Business, using the business name Logo Boosters, and listing nearly $80,000 in net profit. Jackson did not file a 2019 Form 1040. Jackson received the PPP load deposit of $16,628 on March 15, 2021.
Jackson dba WCS Consulting, submitted another PPP loan application less than two weeks later, on March 24, 2021. This contained false statements and documentation.
According to the DoJ, a review of Jackson’s bank records showed she did not open the bank account until March 16, 2021, and used the same social security number belonging to a minor to open the account. As with her business, Logo Boosters, Jackson provided a false 2019 Schedule C with the business name WCS Consulting, listing a net profit of $53,900, and she did not file a 2019 Form 1040. Jackson completed and signed a PPP Loan Forgiveness Application Form on October 5, 2021, indicating that she had complied with all requirements of the PPP rules.
The total loss to the U.S. Government amounted to $43,980 over three PPP loans received by Jackson. She used the proceeds from her fraudulently received loans to purchase jewelry such as tennis bracelets and necklaces, two Rolex watches and a Cartier Santos watch.
The DoJ says Jackson was arrested on January 15, 2025, and released on bond. She pleaded guilty to one count of false statement on a loan or credit application and one count of theft of government property on January 13, 2026.
On Wednesday, U.S. District Judge Christopher Wolfe in Waco sentenced Jackson to serve 21 months in federal prison and pay the $43,980 in restitution. Judge Wolfe also ordered Jackson to forfeit the fraudulently purchased jewelry.
The FBI and IRS Criminal Investigation investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Gregory Gloff prosecuted the case.
